architecturalDecisions.title: Meal-level ingredient snapshot child model
architecturalDecisions.decision: Each meal_plan_recipes entry owns a one-to-many child snapshot collection containing concrete ingredient rows and selection state, preserving meal-specific intent independently from recipe_ingredients.

architecturalDecisions.title: Snapshot identity and reconciliation
architecturalDecisions.decision: Snapshot rows are keyed to source recipe ingredient ids for deterministic reconciliation; new source ingredients auto-append as selected and deleted source ingredients are removed from snapshots.

architecturalDecisions.title: Shared selector and editor contracts
architecturalDecisions.decision: IngredientSelector remains a shared component with explicit mode configuration, while meal-plan ingredient editing state lives in a dedicated MealPlanRecipeIngredientEditor module used by add, edit, bulk review, and quick review surfaces.

architecturalDecisions.title: Single projection pathway
architecturalDecisions.decision: All meal-plan recipe add-to-list actions (bulk and single-meal quick add) call a shared MealPlanToListProjection module that emits grocery stacking inputs from meal snapshots instead of direct recipe_ingredients reads.

architecturalDecisions.title: Override quantity semantics
architecturalDecisions.decision: Snapshot rows track whether quantity is explicitly overridden; overridden quantities remain absolute across servings changes while non-overridden rows continue recipe-based scaling.

architecturalDecisions.title: Legacy compatibility via lazy backfill
architecturalDecisions.decision: Existing meal_plan_recipes records without snapshots are initialized lazily when first entering add-to-list behavior, avoiding an eager migration script.

architecturalDecisions.title: Ownership and permissions alignment
architecturalDecisions.decision: Snapshot entities follow the same grocery-list membership ownership model as meal_plan_recipes so create/update/delete operations are authorized for list members and denied for non-members.

architecturalDecisions.title: Stacking behavior continuity
architecturalDecisions.decision: Meal-plan add-to-list continues using existing metadata-aware stacking behavior, with conflict handling and payload fields preserved while inputs are sourced from snapshot projection.

tickets.title: Add snapshot schema, links, and permission rules
tickets.summary: Introduce a new InstantDB child entity for meal-plan recipe ingredient snapshots, including links to meal-plan recipes and optional store references, plus permission rules aligned with current meal_plan_recipes ownership semantics.
acceptanceCriteria: Schema defines a meal-plan ingredient snapshot entity with fields required to persist full ingredient row values, selection state, source recipe ingredient id, and override metadata
Schema defines a one-to-many link between meal_plan_recipes and snapshot rows with cascade semantics that prevent orphan rows
Schema keeps store linkage optional so existing ingredient-store behavior can be preserved
Permissions allow members with access to the parent meal_plan_recipes row to view/create/update/delete snapshot rows and deny unrelated users
Schema and permissions compile without type errors

tickets.title: Implement snapshot store and lazy backfill contract
tickets.summary: Create MealPlanIngredientSnapshotStore to initialize snapshots from recipe ingredients, reconcile by source ingredient id, and lazily backfill legacy meal entries when snapshot data is missing at add-to-list time.
acceptanceCriteria: Store exposes stable operations to initialize, read, update row selection, update row overrides, and reconcile a meal snapshot
Backfill path creates snapshot rows for legacy meal_plan_recipes entries with no snapshot data only when needed by add-to-list flows
Reconciliation appends newly added source ingredients as selected rows while removing rows whose source ingredient no longer exists
Row order is preserved in recipe ingredient order after initialization and reconciliation
Store logic is reusable from both bulk and single-meal add-to-list pathways
